entries.reason: the 16.4 SDK this package builds against declares it at VTDecompressionSession.h:330 and the release has no such symbol (zero hits for _VTIsHardwareDecodeSupported in the 4.3 and the 6.1.3 armv7 caches), so the port has to export it. It is NOT answered from a table of what this hardware has, because the obvious oracle does not exist at any band: _VTDecompressionSessionCopySupportedPropertyDictionaryForDecoder and its encoder twin are absent from the 4.3, 6.0, 6.1.3, 7.0.1, 10.3.4, 12.0, 16.0 and 18.0 caches alike, so there is no supported-property dictionary to ask
entries.effect: the RELEASE's own answer, asked by trying: a format description is built for the codec with CMVideoFormatDescriptionCreate (CMFormatDescription.h:909, iOS 4.0, which takes the codec type and nothing else, so no parameter sets are needed) and a decompression session is created with kVTVideoDecoderSpecification_RequireHardwareAcceleratedVideoDecoder set to true; such a session exists only if the release can decode that codec in hardware, so YES is noErr from the session create and NO is any failure. The key is the release's own symbol from 4.3 on and this port only declares it, because the 16.4 SDK's VTDecompressionProperties.h puts the whole kVTVideoDecoderSpecification_* block behind #if !TARGET_OS_IPHONE (lines 140-184) while SDK 26.2 declares the key at line 172 with no such guard
entries.source: SDK 26.2, VTDecompressionSession.h:321-331 for the declaration; the per-band ladder from tools/corpus/dump-cache.lua over ~/.charon/dyld/4.3/dyld_shared_cache_armv7 and the 6.1.3 dump, and coordination/corpus/caches/*.tsv; this host's own answers (H264 1, HEVC 1, MPEG2 0, JPEG 1, ProRes422 1, AV1 1, VP9 0) in the facts page

entries.reason: the 16.4 SDK declares it at VTVideoEncoderList.h:60 and the release has no such symbol (zero hits for _VTCopySupportedPropertyDictionaryForEncoder in the 4.3 and the 6.1.3 armv7 caches), so the port has to export it. Everything it returns is the RELEASE's own and is asked for rather than assembled: the encoder ID is the compression session's kVTCompressionPropertyKey_EncoderID read back through the release's VTSessionCopyProperty, and the property dictionary is the release's VTSessionCopySupportedPropertyDictionary for that session
entries.effect: the release's key set with the release's per-key attribute dictionaries - measured on this host, 2026-10-03: H264 gives 140 keys with 0 NULL values, each value an attribute dictionary such as { PropertyType = Number; ReadWriteStatus = ReadWrite; } of which 45 are the EMPTY dictionary; HEVC 169 with 43 empty; ProRes422 59 with all 59 empty; JPEG 54 with 52 empty. A codec with NO encoder answers kVTCouldNotFindVideoEncoderErr (-12908) with no encoder ID and no dictionary, measured for MPEG2 and AV1, and NOT an empty dictionary; kVTParameterErr for a width or height of zero or less
entries.source: SDK 26.2, VTVideoEncoderList.h:55-64 for the declaration and VTErrors.h:37 for -12908; the release's own VTSessionCopyProperty (VTSession.h:112) and VTSessionCopySupportedPropertyDictionary, both present in the 4.3 and the 6.1.3 caches
